harry: Heads-up: in the migration guide clicking the in-page anchor for the "Run" section jumps to the fenced codeblock instead of the H2. Repro in PR: https://git/redwood-inference/docs/pull/2664 :thinking_face:
mina: can you paste a minimal repro?
harry: yep, super small:

```markdown
## Run
Brief description here.
```bash run-example
./deploy.sh --fast
```
[Run](#run)

harry: when you click the link it scrolls to the code fence. Noticed it on both the local dev server and the published site.
gabriel: odd. the fence info string ("bash run-example") is probably being slugified and the renderer is assigning an id to the fence element. if the slug matches the heading slug, the browser may land on the first matching id, which in this case is the fence.
mina: short-term workaround is to add an explicit id on the heading: `## Run {#run}`. awkward but effective.
gabriel: long-term we should prevent code fences from generating ids or at least prefer heading ids during post-processing.
harry: I pushed the heading-id patch to the PR so CI can re-run.
docs-bot: Note: add a style-guide item "prefer explicit heading ids when adjacent to code fences with info-strings".
ci-bot: CI: docs build started for PR #2664
ci-bot: CI: docs linkcheck failed (anchor resolved to code fence) - full log: https://ci.redwood-inference/builds/8032
gabriel: filing DOCS-872 to update the markdown pipeline: change slug behavior so fences don't claim ids, and add a linkcheck assertion that anchors point to headings not code blocks. assigning to docs-infra.
infra-bot: DOCS-872 created and assigned to @gabriel (priority: medium).
mina: for author ergonomics we could also strip the extra tokens from fence info strings before slugging (i.e., only use the language token for fences). but that might be a breaking change; add to RFC.
harry: thanks all, merging the patch with explicit id now and following up on DOCS-872. :shipit:
